thread:
customer_jones: Hi team — started seeing a bunch of failures from our production job calling /v1/functions/invoke. Errors started after we upgraded the SDK to 2.5.0 yesterday. Examples below, request id: req_84a3f. Can you help?

customer_jones: Curl we use (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/functions/invoke \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"function":"processOrder","args":{"order_id":"ORD-4432","priority":2,"items":{"sku":"A123","qty":3}}}'
```

customer_jones: Response we get (500 / structured output parse error):
```json
{"error":"StructuredOutputError","message":"invalid function args: field 'priority' expected enum string [low,medium,high] but got number; field 'items' expected array but got object","request_id":"req_84a3f"}
```

maria_support: Sorry about that — thanks for the repro. Quick q: are you calling with json_mode=strict anywhere, or using SDK helper that sets structured_output=true?

customer_jones: We do set json_mode=strict in the SDK ini. No custom middleware. This only started after SDK 2.5.0 upgrade. Before that calls succeeded.

maria_support: Hmm. Two things to debug: 1) enum coercion (int -> string) should have been rejected earlier too, so maybe the runtime changed how it validates. 2) items shape — looks like previously our helpers coerced single-item objects into arrays for convenience and that behavior might have been removed. I can escalate to eng but can you share the raw request body bytes and SDK version header if possible?

customer_jones: Pasted the raw bytes above — that's the exact payload. SDK sent header: X-Redwood-SDK: client-js/2.5.0. Also seeing intermittent 401s for a small subset of calls right before the 500s:
```json
{"error":"Unauthorized","message":"token expired","request_id":"req_84a3d"}
```

maria_support: Thanks. Retries on 401 could be triggering duplicate attempts which bump your billing; I see a billing spike tied to retries for your org id org_9921 in our logs. We'll include that in the escalation.

maria_support: Escalating to eng-ml and eng-sre. Pinging. @todd_eng @kyle_sre — customer reports schema drift after SDK upgrade: enum now rejected (number vs string) and single-object items no longer coerced into array. Also intermittent 401s and a billing increase due to retries. Request IDs: req_84a3d, req_84a3f.

ops-bot: new escalation created: INC-2023-2247 assigned to eng-ml, eng-sre. Priority: high.

todd_eng: assigning myself. Can you paste the full function schema you registered for processOrder? Need to confirm declared types.

customer_jones: Function schema from our dashboard (copied):
```json
{"name":"processOrder","args":{"order_id":"string","priority":{"type":"enum","values":["low","medium","high"]},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"sku":"string","qty":"integer"}}}}
```

todd_eng: Schema looks right. The payload you sent violates it: priority is number (2) and items is object not array. Two hypotheses: 1) SDK 2.5.0 stopped auto-coercing client-side (int -> "2" or wrapping object into [obj]) and now it submits raw payloads which the runtime validates strictly. 2) Runtime validation changed in a recent deploy and is now stricter when json_mode=strict.

kyle_sre: I pulled the service deploy history — there was a small change last night to structured-output validation in the compiler layer (made enum checks strict for json_mode=strict). Rollout was canaryed but looks like the canary window overlapped some production traffic. I'll roll back that change on canary and confirm impact.

maria_support: For a short-term mitigation for the customer: 1) downgrade SDK to 2.4.x which preserves previous coercion behavior OR 2) modify request to match schema (priority: "medium" replace numeric; items: [ { ... } ] ). Which is feasible for you?

customer_jones: Downgrade is risky for us. We can change the client to stringify enums and ensure items is an array in the next deploy. How quickly can you confirm rollback? We have time-sensitive orders impacted.

kyle_sre: I'll revert the strict-enum change on canary within 30m and promote if we see errors regress. I'll patch the logging to include the SDK header so we can correlate future regressions.

todd_eng: Also opening an internal ticket to add a non-breaking coercion layer when json_mode is not 'strict' and clearer error messages describing expected shape to help debugging.

maria_support: Logged workaround for you: if you add a small pre-hook in your client to coerce priority numbers to enum strings (1->"low",2->"medium",3->"high") and ensure items is always an array, you should stop seeing 500s. Example snippet: 
```js
// normalize before calling
if (typeof body.args.priority === 'number') {
  const map = {1:'low',2:'medium',3:'high'};
  body.args.priority = map[body.args.priority] || 'medium';
}
if (!Array.isArray(body.args.items)) {
  body.args.items = [body.args.items];
}
```

customer_jones: Thanks, we'll ship that hotfix in ~45 minutes. Please confirm when canary is rolled back. Also can you confirm the billing spike will be reviewed?

maria_support: Confirmed — eng-sre will revert canary and post back in this thread. I've opened a billing review request referencing your org id and the retry-related spikes; billing team will follow up within 24 hours.

ops-bot: INC-2023-2247 updated: canary rollback initiated by kyle_sre.

kyle_sre: Canary rollback done. Monitoring metrics now — structured-output error rate for processOrder down ~92% in the last 10m. No new 401 surges detected after rollback, will continue to monitor for 1h.

maria_support: Great. Leaving this open until your hotfix is live and billing team confirms. Anything else you need?

customer_jones: That's perfect, thanks everyone. We'll post once our fix is deployed. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
